LESSON: DRESSING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Myself
Topic 1.4: Dressing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Dressing, part of Myself in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we dress on clothes?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Dressing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner learns independently when dressing and undressing dolls.

Values:
Unity: learner teams up to sort and group clothes according to different weather conditions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Child’s rights: learner understands own rights as one values own clothes.

Link to other learning area:

Dressing and undressing dolls relates to concepts of sorting and grouping in Mathematical activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Large pictures on dressing mounted on heavy gauge pieces of paper, video clips and pictures of clothes worn in and out of

school, A theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices with special accessibility features and

software, head/ mouth pointers, universal cuffs with padded pencils, cut out pictures about clothes worn during different weather

conditions, a doll, assorted clothes (sweater, jackets, shirts, shorts, skirts, blouses), velcro-fastening clothes, clothes with elastic

band, dressing stick (dressing aid), button-hook, magnetic buttons, zipper-helper, shoe horn/ shoe helper, sock slider, shoe

fastener and Lace aids, clothes worn in and out of school, chart on clothes worn at home and school

Other related service providers: Physiotherapist, Learner support Assistant/ Scribe
